title: When the Passage Breaks
premise: Casper Sterling, a salvage diver drowning in debt to a ruthless harbor broker, is hired quietly by a naval officer to recover a sealed strongbox from a wreck the fleet officially denies exists. When the officer's upriver expedition goes silent and Casper's own compass begins pointing somewhere impossible, he realizes the wreck holds more than salvage—it holds proof of what happened to the missing expedition. Racing the salvage fleet upriver across six tides, Casper must choose between paying his debt with the box's contents or exposing the truth that would destroy the man who saved his father's life. He opens the box, gives the truth to the expedition's last survivor, and walks away with nothing but the compass—and finally free.
about_author: Edmund Okafor is a former merchant marine who spent a decade working coastal salvage before turning to fiction full-time. He writes adventure novels from a houseboat, drawing on real wrecks, real tides, and the people who make their living beneath them.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Diving a forbidden wreck at dawn, Casper surfaces to find a naval lieutenant waiting on his boat with an offer: recover a sealed strongbox, debts forgiven, questions unasked. The emotional beat is wary temptation—Casper knows offers like this always cost more than they pay, but the broker's deadline looms.

chapters.title: The Broker's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. In port, Casper endures a humiliating meeting with Marek Voss, the harbor broker who owns his debt, and learns Voss has already heard rumors of the navy job. The beat is claustrophobic pressure—every escape route Casper maps ends at Voss's ledger or the fleet's guns.

chapters.title: Static on the River
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Preparing to dive, Casper monitors the expedition's radio channel out of habit and hears it dissolve into static mid-sentence. He reports it; the navy denies any expedition exists. The beat is dread—the lie confirms everything, and now he's the only one who knows they're missing.

chapters.title: Compass North
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. His father's old compass, dead for years, begins swinging toward the river mouth on its own. Casper tests it against every instrument he owns; only the compass disagrees, steadily, impossibly. The beat is eerie wonder—inheritance as summons, pulling him toward a choice he hasn't made yet.

chapters.title: The Fleet Weighs Anchor
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Casper and Ilsa Reyes, a rival salvager who once loved him. The salvage fleet mobilizes after an anonymous tip—Voss's doing—and Ilsa must decide whether to race them or warn Casper. The beat is divided loyalty; she chooses neither, choosing instead to run her own race.

chapters.title: Upriver in the Dark
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Running the river at night, past checkpoints and snags, Casper finds the expedition's abandoned camp—torn tents, a journal page naming the strongbox, drag marks leading into the water. The beat is mounting horror transformed into resolve: this stopped being a job pages ago.

chapters.title: What the Wreck Keeps
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Diving the true wreck below cold black water, Casper finds the strongbox open and empty beside the expedition leader's body—and a survivor hiding in an air pocket, half-mad, clutching documents that prove the navy sank its own ship to bury a scandal. The beat is terrible clarity.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Wake
chapters.summary: POV: Ilsa. Ilsa catches up, finds Casper's boat adrift, and must choose between the fleet's bounty and the man she never stopped watching. She finds him and the survivor, and instead of turning them in, burns her own contract. The beat is love rekindled through shared defiance.

chapters.title: The Sixth Tide
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Cornered at the river mouth by Voss's men and the fleet as the last tide turns, Casper trades the documents' location to the one honest officer left, letting the truth surface publicly while Voss's leverage collapses. The beat is sacrificial climax—he wins by giving up the prize.

chapters.title: Debt of Salt
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Weeks later, debt-free but penniless, Casper repairs his boat while Ilsa negotiates them a legitimate charter. The compass finally points true north and stays there. The beat is quiet resolution: survival cost him everything he carried, and left him everything that mattered.
